Continue from [CPW inputs](aedt-inputs.qmd) for the public dimensions and PDK
materials. That lesson's GDS mapping is for ordinary HFSS; current Q3D accepts
explicit body geometry under `scgsim.aedt.q3d.v3`. This source-free example
declares the CPW outlines and their finite Z intervals directly. It does not
import or convert the shared GDS.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import (
    MatrixRunControl, Q3dBodySpec, Q3dNetSpec, Q3dSpec, prepare_handoff,
)

bodies = (
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="signal",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, -5.0), (250.0, -5.0),
                     (250.0, 5.0), (-250.0, 5.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=0.0, z_max_um=0.2,
        material_id="Nb", physical_role="signal", net_id="Signal",
    ),
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="ground_upper",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, 11.0), (250.0, 11.0),
                     (250.0, 91.0), (-250.0, 91.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=0.0, z_max_um=0.2,
        material_id="Nb", physical_role="ground", net_id="Ground",
    ),
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="ground_lower",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, -91.0), (250.0, -91.0),
                     (250.0, -11.0), (-250.0, -11.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=0.0, z_max_um=0.2,
        material_id="Nb", physical_role="ground", net_id="Ground",
    ),
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="substrate",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, -91.0), (250.0, -91.0),
                     (250.0, 91.0), (-250.0, 91.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=-500.0, z_max_um=0.0,
        material_id="Si", physical_role="substrate", net_id=None,
    ),
)
nets = (
    Q3dNetSpec("Signal", "Signal", ("signal",),
                "signal", "-X", "signal", "+X"),
    Q3dNetSpec("Ground", "Ground", ("ground_upper", "ground_lower")),
)
spec = Q3dSpec(
    project_name="public_cpw_q3d",
    design_name="CpwFiniteGroundQ3d",
    materials=materials, vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    bodies=bodies, nets=nets,
    run_control=MatrixRunControl("Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3),
    region_padding_um=(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 1000.0),
    solve_ac_rl=True,
)
handoff = prepare_handoff(spec=spec, output_dir=Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-q3d"))
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.archive_path)
```

The Signal net names the signal body and its `-X` and `+X` terminal faces;
the Ground net owns both separate ground bodies without terminals. Together
the nets cover every conductor body exactly. For a C/G-only request, set
`solve_ac_rl=False` and omit the Signal terminal pair. The public example's
6 GHz frequency and three-pass limit are study inputs. Preserve actual
extraction criteria, any changes and native completion/convergence status in
your study notes.
The [result-reading lesson](returned-results.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use) relates
the selected matrix quantity and its available history to the intended SCQ use;
the native stopping flag alone does not decide its adequacy.

Keep native status, reported delta and actual controls with the matrix result;
the [matrix observation contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations)
describes their retention. Judge whether the matrix quantity and available
changes support the accuracy your intended study needs.

## Know which formulation you requested

The default `solve_ac_rl=True` requests combined capacitance/conductance and
AC resistance/inductance. The complete return seals native `c_matrix.csv`,
`ac_rl_matrix.csv` and normalized `matrices.csv` under `results/q3d/`.

For a capacitance/conductance-only study, create a separate spec with
`solve_ac_rl=False`. That formulation returns only native `c_matrix.csv`; it
creates no AC-RL setup or compatibility matrix artifact. A dedicated grounded
Region enclosure is an additional optional model choice on that CG-only spec:
`grounded_region_net="EnclosureGround"`, where the new net name differs from
all physical nets. It requests six native PEC face sheets and preserves the
physical Ground nets. It does not unite the sheets, add bridges or claim an
AC/DC return path. The [contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q3d-extraction-and-region-ground-candidate)
owns native validation/readback and the distinction between enclosure and
physical ground.

Review body outlines, Z intervals, exact Net membership and extraction choice
as request inputs. This example prepares the portable v3 request; it does not
demonstrate native body import, solve or matrix readback. The body-v3 native
lowering remains **CONVERGING**. The
[matrix observation contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations)
describes retained output for a complete return. Changing enclosure or
extraction formulation creates a different experiment, not an offline loss
update to old results.

## GeometryPlan-backed C/G preparation

The shared [Xmon input lesson](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd) prepares an
immutable `snapshot` with its final Net assignments. The structured v3
frontend consumes that snapshot for a C/G-only handoff. Supply one
`PdkMaterial` per source material ID in `materials`; this explicit mapping
preserves source material identity and selects each declared AEDT library
record. The frontend creates v3 body records; it does not use the source-free
body declarations in the CPW example above.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import MatrixRunControl, prepare_q3d_from_geometry

handoff = prepare_q3d_from_geometry(
    snapshot,
    output_dir=Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-q3d-cg"),
    project_name="public_xmon_q3d_cg",
    design_name="PublicXmonQ3dCg",
    materials=materials,
    net_types={"xmon_pad": "Signal", "Ground": "Signal"},
    physical_ground_nets=("Ground",),
    run_control=MatrixRunControl(
        "Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3,
    ),
    region_padding_um=(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 1000.0),
)
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.archive_path)
```

The example keeps the caller's final Net IDs and explicitly classifies the
physical `Ground` role while requesting native `Signal` matrix rows for both
Nets. It creates no terminals or locator-sheet geometry and performs no
connectivity inference. Source coordinates, complete outer and inner rings,
Z intervals, materials, final Nets and available source lineage are retained
in the v3 bodies and `geometry_source` attachment; the canonical snapshot GDS
remains unchanged. The body/native lowering contract is **CONVERGING** and
has not been demonstrated by a native import, solve or matrix readback.
Source curves remain outside the current AEDT lowering contract.

An optional native build-only source candidate uses the existing CLI with a
prepared Q3D v3 handoff: `python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only`
(substitute the directory returned by `prepare_q3d_from_geometry`). It prepares
and reads back the native model, saves the project and releases its owned
Desktop without calling `Analyze` or exporting C/G matrices. This consumes the
one-shot handoff; prepare a new handoff before a later solve. Native behavior is
not yet observed, and the normal `--execute` path is unchanged. The
[Q3D contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q3d-body-input-v3) describes the
receipt and strict-resolution boundary.

Use the existing `aedt-epr` installation extra when preparing this structured
GDSFactory/KLayout source. Source-free `Q3dSpec` bodies need no GDS import.
Configured resource values are recorded run inputs; they do not by themselves
guarantee a hard process-memory cap or report an independently observed
effective solver allocation.
